To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the characteristics of user-created playlists can be described by a set of musical and meta-data properties and that the characteristics of such user-created playlists are different from those of playlists generated by today’s online playlisters and from those of playlists created by a nearest-neighbor playlisting technique.

(i) popularity, freshness and homogeneity are important factors for users when creating playlists manually, (ii) the quality of user-created playlists is different from automatically created ones, and (iii) the quality of automatically generated playlists is different from user-generated playlists.

(1) user-generated playlists are often more homogeneous and diverse than playlists created by algorithms and (2) the quality of user-created playlists can be improved by considering popularity, freshness and similarity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the characteristics of shared playlists and their relation to user preferences.
the question how to improve the quality of automatically created playlists by taking into account the user preferences and the desired characteristics of such playlists.
the question which characteristics of shared playlists are most important for their acceptance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

today’s online services do a good job in generating playlists that are similar to the ones that users create themselves, but they could still improve in terms of the freshness and diversity of the generated tracks.
there is a certain demand for a better understanding of the characteristics of shared playlists in order to design better algorithms for automated playlist generation.
the quality criteria for playlisting algorithms should be extended with additional factors like freshness and diversity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the generation of playlists is a complex process that is not only based on musical factors but also on the user’s preferences and the context of the playlist generation.
the quality criteria for playlists are still not fully understood and that there is still much work to be done in this field.
we found some interesting differences between automatically generated and user-created playlists, but that the question of what makes a good playlist remains open.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is still a lot of room for research on better playlisting algorithms that generate playlists that users actually like.
the characteristics of user-generated playlists should be considered more strongly when developing and evaluating music playlisting algorithms in the future.
we need to take a closer look at the characteristics of user-created music playlists in order to design better music playlisting algorithms.
